body:
Added src/fmt.c/fmt.h + parena fmt [-w] <file.prn>... subcommand. Text-level re-indenter (not AST round-trip -- ast.h has no comment nodes, comments are dropped entirely during lexing, so an AST-based pretty-printer would silently delete every ;; doc comment in this stdlib). Tracks paren/bracket/brace depth, correctly skips over string literals and line comments (matching lexer.c's own escape/comment rules exactly), re-indents each line to depth*2 spaces. Verified: comments/strings survive verbatim, output re-parses and re-compiles (tested against stdlib/string.prn -- still gcc-clean after formatting), idempotent (formatting twice = formatting once). Real, honest scope: depth-based, not semantic Lisp-style alignment (a hand-aligned multi-line loop binding vector gets flattened to the mechanical depth indent, not preserved) -- flagged in fmt.c's own header comment.

⚓ ☃
title: parena fmt -- gofmt-style auto-formatter
